limitations.statement: Process loss is simulated in-process by raising at a named durability boundary and then reopening the store. It reproduces the loss of all in-memory state, but not signal delivery, partially flushed operating-system buffers, or a kill between the write and the fsync return.
limitations.boundary: A real SIGKILL harness would need a subprocess-per-phase runner, which this unit did not build.

limitations.statement: Durability relies on the platform honouring fsync on the journal and sink files. A filesystem or virtual device that reorders or discards fsync would break the crash argument, and this unit cannot detect that.
limitations.boundary: Filesystem write-barrier behaviour is not observable from the producer runtime.

limitations.statement: The mechanism assumes a single writer per store. Concurrent processes appending to the same journal are not fenced by a file lock, so a multi-writer race is out of scope and untested.
limitations.boundary: Wave A dispatch gives each producer an isolated worktree and store, so a single writer is the deployed condition; the general case remains unproven.

limitations.statement: The external effect sink is a local append-only log standing in for a real external system. Exactly-once is proven for the sink's own record surface, not for an external service that could itself duplicate or lose a call.
limitations.boundary: Any real sink must expose an idempotency key with the same semantics; this unit proves the caller side only.

limitations.statement: The journal grows without bound. There is no compaction, snapshotting or retention rule, so startup cost is linear in the number of records ever written.
limitations.boundary: Acceptable at Wave A scale; compaction would reintroduce a second durable object and was deliberately rejected (RJ-PO03-WA-015-001).

limitations.statement: A retriable refusal appends one evidence record per delivery attempt, so a sender that redelivers an out-of-order callback indefinitely grows the journal indefinitely. There is no backoff or attempt cap.
limitations.boundary: No transition or external effect results, so the correctness claim is unaffected; only storage is.

limitations.statement: Callback authenticity is not verified. The mechanism enforces role, identity, fence and ordering discipline over a declared actor string; it does not authenticate that the sender is who the string says.
limitations.boundary: Authentication belongs to the transport, which this unit does not own and did not touch.

limitations.statement: Lease expiry is not driven by a clock. Fencing is proven for explicit lease transfer; a lease that merely times out without a transfer callback is not modelled.
limitations.boundary: Introducing a clock would break the byte-identical determinism the recurrence test depends on; a logical expiry callback would be the deterministic alternative.

limitations.statement: The requested configuration claude-opus-5-thinking-high with high reasoning was not observable as an exact runtime value. The runtime self-identifies as Claude Opus 5 and the enclosing cloud-agent record reports originalModelName gpt-5.6-sol-max-fast for the parent run; no field exposes an effective reasoning level.
limitations.boundary: Recorded as observed without inference in result/result.json runtime_observation; the exact requested slug is not claimed as observed.

limitations.statement: Wall time as the dispatching controller would measure it is not available. Only a locally observed work window is recorded.
limitations.boundary: The producer runtime does not expose the controller dispatch clock; token and cost data are likewise unavailable.

limitations.statement: Independent acceptance is NOT_TESTED. This producer verified its own artifacts by immutable remote readback but did not and may not accept its own result, and did not record COMPLETED.
limitations.boundary: Only the coordinator may record COMPLETED, and a different producer must accept or reject; the custody document keeps completion_actor null and independent_acceptance.state NOT_TESTED.
